In the question given below, a passage/statement is given followed by three statements which may or may not strengthen/weaken the assertion made in the passage. Answer the questions as per the individual direction given.

 

By giving a Chinese rice variety a second copy of one of its own genes, researchers have boosted its yield by up to 40%. The change helps the plant absorb more fertiliser, boosts photosynthesis, and accelerates flowering, all of which could contribute to larger harvests. The government plans to allow the sowing of the modified variety in arid northern states from the next season.

Which of the following, if true, would weaken the above argument?

I. Farmers in the northern states use cheap but less nutrient-dense manure from domesticated animals in place of fertilisers.
II. The modified variety requires 20% more water per hectare.
III. The country’s long-term food security is at risk due to extreme weather events.
questions.explanation: The passage tells us how the government plans to introduce a genetically modified variety of rice in dry northern states due to its higher yield which it attains by absorbing more fertiliser and accelerating flowering. I tell us how farmers in the northern states use manure (which has less nutrients) instead of fertilisers, and will weaken the given argument as the modified variety requires more fertiliser for better growth and yield. II tells us how the modified variety requires more water and weakens the argument about cultivating it in arid areas. Thus, Option 2 is the right answer.

options:

\)

Total blue colour balls \(=5 x\)
Total red and green colour balls \(=24 x-5 x=19\)
Total red colour balls \(=19 x \times\left(\frac{9}{19}\right)=9 x\)

Total green colour balls \(=19 x \times\left(\frac{10}{19}\right)=10 x\)
From I:
Average of total number of balls of all the three colours-
\[

& \frac{5 x+9 x+10 x}{3}=8 \\
& 24 x=24 \\
& x=1
\end{aligned}
\]

Total balls in the bag \(=24 x=24\)
Statement I alone is sufficient.
From II:
Probability that two drawn balls are of green
\[

\end{aligned}

Total balls in the bag \(=24 x=24\)

Statement II alone is sufficient.

Probability that one ball is drawn and that ball is either red or blue-

questions.question: Which three organizations signed a tripartite MoU on June 10, 2025, to combat road dust pollution in the National Capital Region (NCR)?

CAQM, TERI, and Indian Green Building Council

On June 10, 2025, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) entered into a tripartite agreement with CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CRRI) and the School of Planning and Architecture (SPA), New Delhi, to address road dust—a major source of air pollution in the National Capital Region (NCR). questions.question: Where was India's first hydrogen-powered train coach successfully tested?

questions.question: What is the name of India’s first vertical lift sea bridge inaugurated by PM Modi?

questions.question: What is the primary goal of the “Saksham Niveshak” campaign launched by Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (IEPFA)?

Facilitating KYC updates and dividend claim awareness among shareholders

questions.question: Which startup has been approved by SEBI to test fractional share trading in its innovation sandbox?

questions.question: What is the maximum Central Financial Assistance (CFA) that can be provided per drone package under the 'Namo Drone Didi' scheme?

questions.question: According to the RBI’s Gazette notification dated May 21, 2025, how many members are included in the newly constituted Payments Regulatory Board (PRB)?
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: C. 6.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) officially notified the formation of the Payments Regulatory Board (PRB) via a Gazette notification on May 21, 2025. This board replaces the earlier Board for Regulation and Supervision of Payment and Settlement Systems (BPSS).

The PRB will consist of six members, including:

  • The RBI Governor as the Chairperson (ex officio)

  • The Deputy Governor in charge of Payment and Settlement Systems (ex officio)

  • One RBI official nominated by the Central Board (ex officio)

  • Three nominees from the Central Government

This marks a significant change by including government nominees for the first time, aiming to enhance regulatory oversight while maintaining the RBI’s control over payment systems. The Principal Legal Adviser of the RBI will be a permanent invitee, and domain experts in payment systems, IT, and law can be invited as permanent or ad hoc invitees. The PRB is required to meet at least twice a year.

Historically, in 2018, the government proposed an independent payment regulator via an inter-ministerial panel led by the Economic Affairs Secretary. However, the RBI opposed this move through a Dissent Note, arguing that regulation of payment systems should remain under its jurisdiction for coherence and stability in the financial ecosystem.

Directions: In the question below, three sentences are given, each divided into four parts, in which three parts contain grammatical errors and one part is free from error. Choose the correct part of the sentence.

I. He hadn't paid many attention to any (A)/ woman in many, many year, (B)/ but couldn't helped thinking her one (C)/ of the most attractive he'd ever met (D).

II. I and little sister would take (A)/ you out into the garden, and pick (B)/ the deliciously raspberries and (C)/ a little strawberries for you (D).

III. Because human abilities is distributed (A)/ uneven and technology multiplies the (B)/ ability of the talented, the spread among (C)/ the rich and poor will rise more and more (D).
questions.explanation:
Option (C) is the correct choice.

I - D: The fourth part of the sentence is free from error.

The error in the first part is - MANY is used for countable nouns and MUCH is used for uncountable nouns and ATTENTION is uncountable so MANY is incorrect here.

The error in the second part is - the construction is MANY + PLURAL NOUN so YEAR is incorrect here.

The error in the third part is - The construction is COULD + NOT + BASE form of a verb so is incorrect here.

II - B: The second part of the sentence is free from error.

The error in the first part is - I and LITTLE SISTER need to interchange their positions because the grammatical rules related to the order of personal pronouns, it has to be 2,3,1. The second person in the first place followed by the third person and lastly the first person.

The error in the third part is - We need an adjective to modify the noun RASPBERRIES so DELICIOUSLY is incorrect.

The error in the fourth part is - FEW is used for countable nouns and LITTLE is used for uncountable nouns and STRAWBERRIES is countable so LITTLE is incorrect here.

III - D: The fourth part of the sentence is free from error.

The error in the first part is - ‘IS’ is a singular verb so we need a singular subject so ‘ABILITIES’ is incorrect here.

The error in the second part is - UNEVEN is an adjective and is incorrect because we need an adverb here.

The error in the third part is - only two things are being referred to - the rich and poor. AMONG is used to refer to more than two things, while BETWEEN is used to refer to two things so AMONG is incorrect here.

Hence, the correct answer is option (C).

questions.explanation:
Option (C) is the correct choice.

I - C: The third part of the sentence is free from error.

The error in the first part is - the construction is ‘TO + Base form of a verb’ and ‘INDUCED’ is the past participle of a verb.

The error in the second part is - the construction is ‘TO + Base form of a verb’ and ‘DRANK’ is in the past tense.

The error in the fourth part is - the construction is ‘TO + BE + Past participle of a verb’ and ‘WENT’ is in the past tense.

II - A: The first part of the sentence is free from error.

The error in the second part is - The construction is ‘TO + base form of a verb’ so ‘making’ is incorrect here.

The error in the third part is - the sentence is given in past tense and ‘sees’ is the present form which is incorrect here.

The error in the fourth part is - the sentence is given in past tense and ‘manipulate’ is the present form which is incorrect.

III - A: The first part of the sentence is free from error.

The error in the second part is - AND is connected with similar forms of verb and sentence is in present thus ‘utilized’ is incorrect here.

The error in the third part is - The construction is ‘WILL + base form of a verb’ so ‘seen’ is in the past participle.

The error in the fourth part is - AND is connected with similar forms of verbs and the construction is ‘WILL + base form of a verb’ so ‘influenced’ is in the past participle.

Hence, the correct answer is option (C).

questions.question: Which of the following would be most appropriate as the third sentence in the paragraph?
questions.explanation:

Q comes first as it introduces the just war theory and its two main concerns — when and how war is waged.
Sentence 2 naturally expands on this by naming and briefly defining the two core components — jus ad bellum (right to go to war) and jus in bello (conduct during war).
Sentence T comes next as it's logical to present an additional or modern extension (jus post bellum, which deals with what comes after war) after introducing the two traditional components of just war theory. T expands the framework further, completing the timeline of war ethics (before, during, and after).
After laying out the structure of the theory (Q, 2, T), sentence S provides its underlying moral justification. It shifts from "what the theory includes" to why the theory exists: to weigh the tragedy of war against the possibility of preventing worse outcomes. It connects structure to moral reasoning.
S sets up the idea that war might be a lesser evil in some cases. Sentence 5 follows directly, giving concrete examples of such cases — protecting lives, resisting tyranny, stopping atrocities — thus supporting the ethical basis introduced in S.
Sentence R introduces critics, who oppose or question the justifications supporters make. This provides logical contrast: first supporters’ views, then critics’ objections.
Finally, P pulls together the supporting arguments and criticisms and offers a balanced closing thought emphasizing both acceptance and caution, making it a fitting and meaningful conclusion to the paragraph.
So, the correct order to form a meaningful paragraph is: Q2TS5RP.
Considering the correct order, T would form the third sentence of the paragraph. Hence, option A is the correct answer.

It is true that even at 6.8 or 6.9% this year, India will continue to be the fastest-growing economy in the world. questions.explanation:
The correct word to use in this context should convey that it's not uncommon to observe or witness typical Indian weddings abroad, rather than suggesting that they are not easily noticeable. Therefore, the word "inconspicuous" should be replaced with a word that means "to observe" or "to witness."

Option (1) "Observe, Practices, observe":

"Observe" can replace "follow" to mean that many diaspora members watch or adhere to Indian customs and traditions.
"Practices" can replace "traditions" to signify that they engage in Indian practices.
"Observe" (again) can replace "inconspicuous" to suggest that it's not unusual to discreetly or quietly witness typical Indian weddings abroad.

Option (2) "Emulate, Rituals, witness":

"Emulate" can replace "follow" to convey that many diaspora members imitate or replicate Indian customs and traditions.
"Rituals" can replace "traditions" to emphasize the cultural rituals and ceremonies they participate in.
"Witness" can replace "inconspicuous" to mean that it's not uncommon to openly or openly observe typical Indian weddings abroad.

Option (3) "Pursue, Heritage, notice":

"Pursue" can replace "follow" to indicate that many diaspora members actively pursue Indian customs and traditions.
"Heritage" can replace "traditions" to highlight their cultural heritage and practices.
"Notice" can replace "inconspicuous" to suggest that it's not uncommon to casually or casually notice typical Indian weddings abroad.

In this case, all three options provide suitable replacements for the highlighted words in the original sentence, resulting in improved context and grammar. Therefore, option (D) "All 1,2 & 3" is the correct choice because it offers multiple valid combinations of words that enhance the sentence and correct the grammatical error.
